correctness.rationale: The incidence-tensor decomposition and endpoint-swap edge stabilizer classify the complete S_m x S_n-equivariant projection families. For the cut space P_theta and cycle space Q_s separately, explicit edge-column coefficients yield affine minorants valid for every real parameter, tight on [0,1]. Their unique intersections yield both rational minima for every m,n>=2. Difference factorizations independently establish exact orthogonal exceptions and the impossibility of a complementary optimal pair for unequal factors. The standalone checker reconstructs full matrices and checks images, idempotence, and exact norms for all 36 pairs 2<=m,n<=7, supplementing rather than replacing the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The strongest directly relevant inspected full text is arXiv:2305.12582v1 Section 2.6: its Theorem 43 concerns equal-size homogeneous Hamming factors and unique invariant cycle projections. Its statement and proof do not imply the two unequal-edge-orbit parameterizations, exact separate cut/cycle constants or the exceptional (2,4)/(4,2) orthogonal cycle minima. The 2018 precursor develops invariant averaging for recursive graph families. Published rook-graph homology and cactus basis-projection results have different invariants. Searches by graph name, line-graph equivalence, exact formula, and projection terminology identified no directly dominating published statement. Historical priority is not independently certified.
residual_risks: Historical operator-theoretic or electrical-network literature may give equivalent asymmetric formulas using different terminology.
Several same-object sources were compared only at abstract or indexed-summary level; they were not used for whole-text exclusions.
Mathematical correctness was not independently audited.

value.rationale: The equal-factor Hamming case has an edge-direction exchange symmetry, but standard rectangular rook graphs do not. Resolving that missing symmetry produces a natural complete two-parameter invariant, two distinct sharp nonorthogonal optimizers, an exact classification of when the orthogonal projections stay optimal, and a genuinely exceptional 2-by-4 circulation case. This is structurally motivated by the Banach-space complementation problem, beyond a table of small computations.
